observations: Two large rectangular eye-zones dominate the upper half, each filled with layered red, green, and pink horizontal bands, outlined in heavy black with loose white lines crossing over them.
A wide rectangular mouth zone sits low on the figure, its interior filled with white vertical tooth-shapes separated by black lines, framed by pink and red strokes on a flat purple ground.
Yellow arrow and zigzag shapes cluster at the top edge, mixing with white sawtooth marks and blue strokes, forming a jagged band across the crown of the figure.
reading: The figure is built from stacked rectangles — eye blocks, a narrow nose column, a wide tooth bar — held together by black outlines and then crossed by loose white and pink lines that run over every boundary. The flat purple field keeps the structure from dissolving entirely. The eye zones read as closed or inward; the wide tooth bar below reads as open and exposed, giving the face a double mood: sealed above, bared below.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work shares the stacked-rectangle face structure and tooth-bar mouth visible in title neighbor nnxyz nifty faces #96, but replaces that work's warm orange ground with a flat purple field — the same purple the collector links visually to the nnotb series.

connections.reason: Both works use stacked rectangles and a wide white tooth-bar mouth, but #96 fills its eye zones with bold red X marks on a warm orange ground, making the eyes feel blocked rather than layered.

nnotb #190 shares the same flat purple background — the collector's noted visual link between the two series — but replaces hard rectangles with a rounded, densely scribbled form, a direct contrast in how the purple field is used.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly do the loose white lines cross the black outlines of the eye rectangles, and what happens to the sense of the boundary at those points?
ambiguities: The sawtooth and zigzag marks at the top edge could be read as a separate structural element or as overflow from the eye zones; the image does not resolve this clearly.
nifty faces #98 was inspected but its teal ground and spiral-heavy structure offered no stronger formal connection than the two selected works, so it was omitted.
